bull.b: Life Time has materially improved profitability while scaling revenue, moving from deeply negative margins in 2021 to strong positive operating and net margins in the TTM period. This supports internal funding capacity, strengthens resilience, and gives management more resources to invest in club growth and member services.

Higher dues and growing personal training, spa, and other in-center services show that Life Time is increasing revenue per member rather than relying only on membership volume. A stronger mix of recurring dues and ancillary spending can support durable revenue quality and margin performance.

Raised revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, combined with an active club-opening pipeline, indicates continued confidence in demand and the company’s expansion model. New locations can broaden the membership base and create additional opportunities for recurring dues and higher-margin services over time.

bear.b: Although leverage has improved from 2025, Life Time still carries substantial debt relative to equity. That capital structure can limit flexibility if demand softens, increase sensitivity to borrowing costs, and constrain the amount of internally generated capital available for expansion or other strategic priorities.

bear.t: Negative Free Cash Flow and Heavy Investment
bear.b: Strong operating cash flow is being outweighed by investment needs, leaving free cash flow negative after capital spending. Continued club construction and expansion require substantial funding, which may increase reliance on financing or sale-leasebacks and reduce flexibility until new locations mature.

Membership growth is currently modest, and the intentional reduction in qualified medical memberships lowers reported volume even as it improves mix. Slower unit growth places more pressure on pricing, retention, and ancillary spending to sustain revenue expansion across the next several quarters.
